chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Sadaqa al-Ahdab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Fulfilling the need of a believer is better than freeing a thousand slaves, and better than equipping a thousand horses in the way of Allah.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad — similar to the two hadiths.

key_terms.قَضَاءُ حَاجَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِ: Fulfilling the need of the believer

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of fulfilling a believer's need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi elevates 'qada' al-hajah' (satisfying a believer's need) to a status surpassing major individual acts of worship like freeing slaves or jihad, underscoring its communal significance. Scholars often interpret this as highlighting the practical application of faith through social solidarity, where relieving another's burden is seen as a direct service to God. This emphasis reflects the Imams' focus on strengthening the bonds of 'ukhuwwah' (brotherhood) as a core component of religious duty.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Sadaqa Al Ahdab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:
‘Fulfilling a need of the Momin is better than freeing a thousand necks, and better than loading a thousand horses in the Way of Allahazwj’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad – similar to the two Ahadeeth.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Hakam ibn Ayman from Sadaqah al-Ahdab from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Helping to meet the needs of a believer is better than setting free one thousand slaves and better than donating one thousand horses loaded (with good) in the way of Allah.’’
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Ziyad a Hadith similar to the two above Ahadith.
